claim: This round's §7.4 change makes every port epoch no undo target. V06 still states the older, narrower rule. §7.4 *Replay semantics* (l.10718-10724; VEL0-05): 'Every event of the port's reserved session `host:port` — dossier events, `dossierFacts`, `dossierRecord` and the port's epochs alike, whether or not a port epoch carried a dossier change in `EpochInputs.dossier` — is likewise no `undo`, `redo` or `revert` target'. §7.7 item 3 follows: 'an undo of a lapsing epoch outside the port's session `host:port` restores the hold'. V06 says otherwise in three places. §4.1 (l.3302): 'An epoch that carried a dossier event is never an undo target (§7.4)'. T-V6-27 (l.3866), on H-DOSSIER where every epoch is a port epoch: 'an undo of a lapsing epoch that carried no dossier event restores the hold'. The take-over rows T20-2 and T20-6 (l.3819-3820) say the same. A correct build refuses that undo (F-EDIT), so it fails T-V6-27. A build that follows V06 lets a user undo the host's clock.
required_change: V06 §4.1: replace 'An epoch that carried a dossier event is never an undo target (§7.4)' with 'No event of the port's session `host:port` — a port epoch, with or without a dossier change, a dossier event — is an undo, redo or revert target (§7.4 *Replay semantics*)'. T-V6-27: replace 'and an undo of a lapsing epoch that carried no dossier event restores the hold (T20-2's epoch clause); an `undo` naming an epoch that carried a dossier event returns F-EDIT and changes nothing (T20-6's epoch clause)' with 'and an undo of a lapsing epoch outside the port's session `host:port` (an advance on a what-if copy of the fixture) restores the hold (T20-2's epoch clause); an `undo` naming a port epoch, with or without a dossier change, returns F-EDIT and changes nothing (T20-6's epoch clause)'. Make the take-over rows T20-2 and T20-6 (V06 §7) read the same.

claim: Item 114's recovery order breaks across a history replay. V06 §3.7.7 (3) (l.1599) rebuilds patched runs 'oldest patch first (by the run's last-change epoch, ties in chain order)'. §2.7 (l.2420-2433) has every writer set `conditionEpoch` to 'the epoch in force at its event', 'with the replay the replay's own epochs', and the replay runs item 114's transitions (V06 §3.20.3). §6.1 numbers live epochs 1 … 2³¹ − 1 apart from the replay's range (VAT0-07). After a history-first generation, a run patched in a replay epoch decades ago therefore sorts after a run patched in live epoch 2 if it records `0x8000_0000 + r`, or ties with live epoch r if it records r. Either way the rebuild is not oldest first, and the result is silently wrong.
required_change: In V06 §3.7.7 (3) replace '(by the run's last-change epoch, ties in chain order)' with '(by the week of the run's last-change epoch — `EpochRecord.week` of its `conditionEpoch`, generation's epoch 0 first, a replay epoch's week before every live epoch's, §6.1 — ties in chain order)'. Add to T-V6-73 a history-first fixture: runs patched in replay epochs and in live epochs, recovery rebuilding the replay-era patches first. Add the combination row 'item 114's recovery × the history replay' to V06 §3.21 (b).

claim: g item 122 routes to V06 'the hand-over (aftermath through the epoch path; the camp at the growth frontier; reconstruction as Works)' (item 122 (a); canon's dated ruling for items 121–123). V06 carries none of it: no text names item 122, a crisis look, a camp at the growth frontier, or a look handing over to the next epoch. `ConditionOverlay` is read only for the Works share (V06 §3.13 (6)).
required_change: Write V06's item-122 part at build depth as new design. (1) **The aftermath**: what a crisis leaves reaches the map only through the next epoch — the calamity as an `EpochInputs.events` entry (DR28) run by the hazards phase (V06 §3.11) at its `targets`; deaths and exodus through the population target; newcomers who stay through growth (V06 §3.6). A look never writes an op. (2) **The camp at the growth frontier**: a pure, draw-free query, `frontierFor(doc, households)`: where V06 §3.6's growth would seat that many households next, by the same rules over committed state. It is read by §10.2's refugee-camp placement, so newcomers who stay become the next epoch's suburb where the camp stood. Fallback with no frontier: the approach road by a gate (item 122 (b)). (3) **Reconstruction as Works**: the `reconstruction` archetype's `ConditionOverlay` read by the works phase (V06 §3.13 (6)); a disaster's ruined look ends in the week its rebuild's Works begins, so no week draws both. (4) **Edges and lifecycle rows** (V06 §2.12, V06 §3.21): a look standing when its aftermath epoch folds; a condition with no calamity (a look, no aftermath); the aftermath epoch undone while the look stands; a replay epoch (no look; past calamities reach it as events); a port epoch carrying the calamity. (5) A T-V6 test: the hash identical with crises on and off; the frontier query equal to where the next epoch's growth seats those households on a fixture.

claim: g item 123 routes to V06 'the decay level over time per lineage (existence state, years since abandoned) and restoration' (canon's dated ruling for items 121–123; item 123 (b)). V06 has no decay level. The record that dates a building's abandonment is `Lifecycle.since`, which keeps only the last existence change (§2.8, l.2622). The `decay` Works already carries a dated progress for each step (§4.11 *Works* (4)–(5)), but nothing derives item 123's level from it.
required_change: Write V06's item-123 part at build depth. (1) **The decay level** (0–1) of a building lineage at a week is derived, never stored. It is read from the existing `decay` Works and existence (§4.11 *Works* (4)–(5): `abandoned` and its Works' progress toward `decayed`, then `decayed`, then `ruined`; the dwell bands × 0.6 for timber and thatch being item 123 (b)'s material rate), so the plan's damage and the building's drawn decay stage are one reading. It is monotone while the building stays abandoned, decayed or ruined, and is read at any frame's week (V06 §3.15) and at each replay epoch. (2) **Restoration**: `reoccupy` and a `repair` Works run the stages backwards, so the level falls and the damage leaves in reverse threshold order, a repaired element drawn in patch material (item 114). (3) **Edges** (V06 §3.21): a building generated as a ruin with no Works (its level from its state and V11's default age); a fire's CHARRED state; a successor lineage on a trace (a new plan, level 0); an epoch undone; the replay's first-met ruins (the plan as built, then its damage, item 123 (a)). (4) A T-V6 test: the level is monotone over H-100's decline and falls in reverse on repair.

claim: V06 §6.8 (6) (l. 3763–3767): "A dossier-bound document's epochs are the port's cadence (§4.11 *The clock*) and are never coarsened … each priced at 6.1–6.2 inside §12's waits for a dossier change and an open from SettlementForge." A catch-up folds an epoch at every year end it crosses (§4.11 *The clock* (4): "a catch-up batch follows the same rule"; V08 l. 1778: "every crossing inside the span adds its own epoch"), and a map opened before its turn "catches up at once" (V08 l. 33). By V06 §6.8 (1)'s own rows a catch-up of N years costs ≈ N × 430 ms at CITY (N × 1 120 ms with three islands) and N × 1 310 ms at METROPOLIS (N × 2 090 ms with islands): past ≈ 23 years at CITY (≈ 8 with three islands) and ≈ 7 at METROPOLIS (≈ 4 with islands) its epochs alone exceed the ten seconds item 119 (a) sets for "a dossier change applied" and "open a map from SettlementForge". The claim is unsupported at the limit; V06 §3.21 has no catch-up row and T-V6-24 times none.

V06 §3.21 adds the row "a dossier catch-up of many years | the coarsened catch-up of V06 §6.8 (6) | simpler shape (coarser epochs) | T-V6-24"; T-V6-24 adds a 20-year and a 100-year catch-up at CITY and METROPOLIS, the sky layer off and on, each p95 ≤ 10 000 ms with the dossier's present facts met exactly; a J-V6 row records the choice over keeping the port's cadence.
